question: Does replacing an elementwise-activated Transformer MLP with a pure bilinear gate make its nonlinear computation exactly representable and potentially interpretable through third-order weight tensors and pairwise feature interactions?

key_findings.claim: Author algebra: a bilinear layer (W1 x) elementwise-multiplied by (W2 x) is exactly a quadratic tensor contraction x dot B dot x, with each output slice B_i:: equal to an outer product of the corresponding W1 and W2 rows.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 2-3 match coefficients to obtain B_ijk=W1_ij W2_ik and express B via two weight contractions with a diagonal selector tensor Z. This is an exact reparameterization; B is highly factorized rather than an arbitrary third-order tensor.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer terminology audit: the layer is not linearized with respect to its input; it is a degree-two polynomial represented by multilinear contractions.
key_findings.evidence: The same input x appears twice in x dot B dot x, so scaling x by c scales the output by c squared and additivity fails through cross terms. Tensor contraction is linear in either argument while the other is fixed, but the tied-input map is quadratic. Statements that the nonlinear layer uses 'only linear operations' are defensible as implementation primitives, not as a linear function or ordinary linear circuit.

key_findings.claim: Author path expansion: substituting the bilinear tensor into a one-layer Transformer yields four MLP path families involving zero, one, or two attention-head traversals.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 4-11 expand the residual input into direct and head-mediated paths on both sides of the bilinear product. The resulting terms distinguish direct-direct, attention-direct, direct-attention, and attention-attention contributions before adding direct logits and ordinary attention paths.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer qualification: the Transformer expression is exact but not a fixed linear weight-only circuit because attention matrices remain input-dependent softmax functions, and deeper expansions grow combinatorially.
key_findings.evidence: A_h is defined from token-dependent QK scores. Equation 11 therefore packages, rather than eliminates, attention nonlinearity. Only a one-layer model is expanded; two- and N-layer cases are left as exercises. The formula provides bookkeeping for a chosen input, not by itself a sparse, human-readable causal explanation.

anchors.section: Two- and N-layer expressions left as exercises

key_findings.claim: Author conceptual result: bilinear feature construction decomposes exactly into a sum over ordered pairs of active input features.
key_findings.evidence: For x=sum_i a_i d_i, Equation 15 expands the output into sum_i sum_j a_i a_j d_i dot B dot d_j. This motivates 'additively pairwise nonlinear' feature construction and a modifier/default-feature view with m(x)=W1x modifying W2x.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer qualification: pairwise decomposability does not resolve basis ambiguity, superposition, or scaling by itself.
key_findings.evidence: The note explicitly concedes there is no privileged feature basis and speculates about SVD or ICA. A d_mlp-by-d_model-by-d_model tensor has too many explicit entries to inspect, feature-pair counts can still be quadratic, and transformations of the two factors can preserve function while changing apparent primitives. Proposed coefficient ranking, HOSVD, and feature-selection strategies are not evaluated.

anchors.section: Section 3.2, basis choices and empirical question

key_findings.claim: Reviewer contradiction: the assertion that standard ReLU MLP feature construction is non-decomposable is an informal contrast, not a theorem.
key_findings.evidence: The argument defines a modifier m(x)=ReLU(Wx)/(Wx) and calls using it circular. ReLU networks are nevertheless piecewise linear with explicit activation regions, and exact local Jacobian/path decompositions or input-conditioned gating descriptions exist. Bilinear layers have a globally fixed degree-two expansion, which is simpler in one sense, but the paper does not prove that ordinary MLP circuits cannot be decomposed or interpreted.

key_findings.claim: No experiment is reported; performance and safety implications are inherited or speculative.
key_findings.evidence: The note cites Shazeer's roughly 120M-parameter GLU comparison and explicitly says larger-scale competitiveness is unknown. It trains no model, extracts no feature, tests no tensor decomposition, performs no causal intervention, and ends by describing safety, learning dynamics, and exponentially many feature programs as future possibilities.

anchors.section: Feature construction left as empirical question
Section 3.4, in advance of empirical results

method.core_idea: Rewrite pure bilinear gated MLPs as factorized third-order tensors so their Transformer paths and input-feature interactions can be expanded exactly with multilinear algebra.
method.mechanism: Form B_ijk=W1_ij W2_ik, substitute the quadratic contraction into an attention-plus-MLP residual path expansion, interpret W1x as an input-dependent modifier of W2x, and expand sparse input-feature combinations into pairwise tensor interactions. Suggest SVD/ICA/HOSVD and coefficient prioritization as future interpretability tools.
assumptions: Transformer feed-forward blocks are replaced by pure bilinear gates without GeLU, SiLU, biases, or normalization in the derivation.
A useful feature dictionary exists in which activations are sparse linear combinations.
Large linear maps and third-order tensors are substantially more interpretable than elementwise nonlinear maps.
SVD, ICA, or another chosen basis recovers functionally meaningful default and modifier features despite non-identifiability.
Competitive performance observed for small bilinear/GLU comparisons transfers to models large enough to matter for safety.
Pairwise interaction structure remains tractable despite quadratic feature pairs and deep compositional expansion.

techniques.role: Encode a gated quadratic MLP exactly as a third-order tensor with rank-one output slices.
Separate direct, one-attention-side, and two-attention-side contributions to a one-layer bilinear MLP.
Interpret W1x as linearly modulating default features produced by W2x.
Express output computation as a sum over ordered active-feature pairs.
Propose large coefficients, HOSVD, SVD/ICA, and maximum-modification rankings for future analysis.

evaluations.result: The gated layer equals x dot B dot x exactly for B_ijk=W1_ij W2_ik.
Equation 11 enumerates direct, attention, and four bilinear path families.
evaluations.baseline: Prior attention-only path framework; no empirical circuit recovery.

evaluations.result: The bilinear output decomposes into a sum of pairwise feature tensor contractions.
evaluations.baseline: An informal modifier-vector description of a ReLU MLP.

Author-acknowledged: two- and N-layer Transformer expressions are not derived.

Reviewer-identified: the claimed impossibility/non-decomposability of standard MLP analysis is not established.
failure_modes: Tensor coefficients may be dense, basis-sensitive, and as opaque as the original factors.
A low reconstruction or spectral component may not correspond to a causal semantic feature.
Pairwise interactions can scale quadratically in active features and exponentially after deep composition.
Replacing SiLU/GeLU gates with pure bilinear gates may reduce stability or capability at scale.
Attention input dependence can defeat static path rankings across diverse prompts.
SVD/ICA/HOSVD decompositions can rotate or split under small retraining changes, undermining cross-model comparison.
Weight-only explanations may miss activation distribution, normalization, saturation, and context.
reusable_insights: Polynomial degree is a useful architectural interpretability knob: fixed-degree interactions admit exact tensor expansions.
Store bilinear tensors in factorized form and decompose symmetrized output quadratic forms rather than materializing all entries.
Distinguish exact computational decomposition from semantic interpretability; require causal interventions for the latter.
Report gauge/basis invariances so purported features do not depend on an arbitrary factorization.
Compare architecture-native weight decomposition against post-hoc SAEs/transcoders on faithfulness, sparsity, stability, and behavioral coverage.
Use equal-parameter and equal-compute scaling studies before treating interpretability-friendly architecture changes as drop-in replacements.
open_questions: Do bilinear MLPs match SwiGLU quality and training stability from small models through frontier-scale language models?
Which tensor decomposition is identifiable and stable under equivalent factor transformations?
Can weight-derived components predict and causally control behavior better than SAEs or transcoders?
How fast does exact path count and effective polynomial degree grow with depth and residual composition?
Can sparsity, low rank, quantization, or orthogonality constraints improve interpretability without erasing capability?
What metrics distinguish a human-legible primitive from a merely low-rank spectral direction?
Can an ordinary SwiGLU be locally approximated by bilinear tensors with certified error over the activation distribution?

competitive_landscape.title: GLU Variants Improve Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: Shazeer benchmarks gated feed-forward variants and supplies the performance premise for pure bilinear gating, with SwiGLU generally strongest. Sharkey contributes the tensor/interpretability framing but performs no independent scale or quality experiment.

competitive_landscape.title: Toy Models of Superposition
competitive_landscape.difference: Elhage et al. give controlled empirical/theoretical models of feature superposition and phase changes. The note takes possible combinatorial feature count as motivation and proposes understanding bilinear construction rules, but does not show that this resolves superposition in a trained network.

competitive_landscape.title: Bilinear MLPs Enable Weight-Based Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.difference: Pearce et al., including Sharkey, operationalize this note's proposal with eigendecomposition, toy/image/language models, adversarial examples, overfitting detection, and circuits. It is the empirical validation missing here, though still on modest scales and selected tasks.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Cunningham et al. learn sparse activation features in an existing nonlinear language model and provide automated and causal evidence. Bilinear weight decomposition promises exact model-native computation but requires changing the architecture and solving basis semantics; the approaches trade post-hoc approximation for architectural restriction.

competitive_landscape.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
competitive_landscape.difference: Dunefsky et al. approximate dense MLPs with sparse transcoders and recover feature circuits in 120M-1.4B models. This attacks the same MLP barrier without retraining a bilinear base model, but sacrifices exact equivalence; a direct faithfulness/tractability comparison is an important missing experiment.

competitive_landscape.title: Weight-based Decomposition: A Case for Bilinear MLPs
competitive_landscape.difference: Pearce, Dooms, and Rigg introduce sparse eigendecomposition of bilinear tensors on MNIST and Tiny Stories and report preliminary interpretability. It directly tests the note's weight-based path, while also exposing architecture/parameter and scale trade-offs absent from the note.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Bilinear MLPs extend tensor-style Transformer circuit analysis beyond attention-only models and may enable safety-relevant understanding of how exponentially many features are constructed from primitives.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The note derives an exact factorized third-order tensor, a one-layer path expansion, and a pairwise input-feature interaction formula, then proposes basis/decomposition heuristics.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The concise connection between pure bilinear GLUs, exact quadratic tensors, Transformer path bookkeeping, and feature-construction interpretability is a useful agenda-setting contribution. Bilinear/gated layers and superposition theory predate it, and the work contains no experiment; later same-line papers provide the actual empirical evidence. Its strongest durable result is the exact pairwise tensor representation, while performance, tractability, semantic interpretability, and safety remain hypotheses.

reviewer_notes: All 12 extracted pages were read. Primary competitors and direct successors were checked on arXiv and OpenReview on 2026-08-23. The audit preserves the exact algebra while distinguishing multilinear operations from a linear input-output map and formal decomposition from semantic/causal interpretation.
